questions.question:
Study the graph and answer the question given below:

The given graph represents the number of workers getting daily wages (in Rs.).

Total number of workers = 200

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f9f98d03f23f1008a1881580648e36924c871402ed0b6e3c0ffcddcb88a649c5.png] 

What is the difference between the percentage of workers whose daily wages are less than Rs. 500 and the percentage of workers whose daily wages are Rs. 600 and above?
questions.solution:
**Calculation:**

Total number of workers = 200

The workers whose daily wages are less than Rs. 500 = (20 + 25) = 45

The percentage of workers whose daily wages are less than Rs. 500 = (45/200 × 100)

⇒ 22.5%

The workers whose daily wages are Rs. 600 and above = (40 + 60) = 100

The percentage of workers whose daily wages are Rs. 600 and above = (100/200 × 100)

⇒ 50%

Now,

The difference between the percentage of workers whose daily wages are less than Rs. 500 and the percentage of workers whose daily wages are Rs. 600 and above = (50 – 22.5)%

⇒ 27.5%

**∴ The required difference is 27.5%**

questions.question:
The given histogram shows the frequency distribution of the speed of cars passing though at a particular spot on a highway. Study the graph and answer the question that follows.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/df89242fb618161d84d69a7b04ab21b234c920bcd00fc2b1ae271dd06b55dc64.png] 

What is the ratio of the number of cars with speed less than 60 km / h to the number of cars with speed more than 80 km / h?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Number of cars with speed less than 60 km/h = 50 + 70 = 120

Number of cars with speed more than 80 km/h = 60 + 45 = 105

**Concept used:**

Using the concept of ratio

**Calculation:**

Required ratio = Number of cars with speed less than 60 km/h ∶ Number of cars with speed more than 80 km/h

⇒ Required ratio = 120 ∶ 105

⇒ Required ratio = 8 ∶ 7

**∴ The required ratio is 8 ∶ 7.**

The ratio of the total number of workers whose daily wages are less than Rs. 500 to the total number of workers whose daily wages are more than Rs. 600 is:
questions.solution:
**Calculation:**

The total number of workers whose daily wages are less than Rs. 500 = (20 + 25) = 45

The total number of workers whose daily wages are more than Rs. 600 = (40 + 60) = 100

The ratio of the total number of workers whose daily wages are less than Rs. 500 to the total number of workers whose daily wages are Rs. 600 and above 

⇒ (45 : 100)

⇒ 9 : 20

**∴ The required ratio is 9 : 20**

questions.question:
Study the given histogram that shows the marks obtained by students in an examination and answer the question that follows.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c3bfd6e44a1fd34b512410a3fae7e3ee0057585cf854be00b09bd8fd8fac9de8.png] 

If the total number of students is represented as a pie chart, then the central angle corresponding to students whose marks are more than 250 but less than 300 is?

(correct to the nearest degree)
questions.solution:
**Calculation:**

Total number of students = 30 + 45 + 60 + 35 + 40 +35

⇒ Total number of students = 245

And students whose marks are more than 250 but less than 300 = 60

But 245 students represents 360° 

⇒ 1 student = 360° /245

⇒ 60 students = (360° /245) × 60

⇒ 60 students = 88.16° 

**∴ The nearest value for students corresponding to 250 or more but lesser than 300 is 88° .**

questions.question:
The histogram shows the marks scored by 40 students in a test with maximum 30 marks.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f1466743501f52623265348a1481f925c546de183a03e5ce928a08d45d28bcf3.png] 

What is the percentage of the students who scored less than 20 marks?
questions.solution:
**Calculation:**

The total number of students who scored less than 20 marks = (2 + 8 + 7 + 8) = 25

Total number of students = 40

The percentage of the students who scored less than 20 marks = (25/40 × 100)

⇒ 125/2

⇒ 62.5%

**∴ The required percentage is 62.5**

questions.question:
The following histogram represents the daily earnings of 50 medical stores in a locality.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/bf54b685240f27894c6f8f572a209d5b2af66f833e4379903c3c6f3b61b946ee.png] 

The difference between the percentage of medical stores whose daily earnings are less than Rs. 1,000 and the percentage of medical stores whose daily earnings are Rs. 1,200 and above is:
questions.solution:
**Calculation:**

The total number of medical stores = 50

The medical stores whose daily earning are less than Rs. 1000 = (16 + 10) = 26

The percentage of medical stores whose daily earning are less than Rs. 1000 = (26/50 × 100) = 52

The medical stores whose daily earning are Rs. 1200 and more = (8 + 6 + 4) = 18

The percentage of medical stores whose daily earning are Rs. 1200 and more = (18/50 × 100) = 36

Now,

The difference between the percentage of medical stores whose daily earnings are less than Rs. 1,000 and the percentage of medical stores whose daily earnings are Rs. 1,200 and above

⇒ (52 – 36)%

⇒ 16%

**∴ The required difference is 16%**

questions.question:
**Direction:** Study the following histogram and answer the given question.

A study was made for the number of persons of different age group visited in a library in a week which is shown in given in the histogram. Study the histogram and answer the question given below.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/07efa484cd023979145f99e9c3f561db8e60e7398fc8b8c19647567d75990e70.png] 

What percent of the total number of persons visiting library in the week was the number of persons of age group 25 - 30 years?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Number of persons of age group 15-20 = 300 years 

Number of persons of age group 20-25 = 400 years 

Number of persons of age group 25-30 = 200 years 

Number of persons of age group 30-35 = 350 years 

Number of persons of age group 35-40 = 100 years 

Number of persons of age group 40-45 = 50 years 

Number of persons of age group 45-50 = 200 years 

**Formula used:**

If a person age is x years and the total age of members is y years 

then a person percentage age in total = (x/y)× 100

**calculation:**

total age of persons = 300 + 400 + 200 + 350 + 100 + 50 + 200

⇒ 1600 years 

∴ percentage age of group 25-30 = (200/1600) × 100

⇒ (1/8) × 100

⇒ 12.5%.

**Hence, the percentage age of group 25-30 will be 12.5%.**

questions.question:
Study the given histogram that shows the marks obtained by students in an examination and answer the question that follows.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c3bfd6e44a1fd34b512410a3fae7e3ee0057585cf854be00b09bd8fd8fac9de8.png] 

The number of students who obtained less than 350 marks is what per cent more than the number of students who obtained 400 or more marks?

(correct to one decimal place)
questions.solution:
Calculation:

Number of student obtained less than 350 = (30 + 45 + 60 + 35) = 170

Number of student obtained 400 or more = 35

Difference between number of students obtained less than 350 and number of students obtained 400 or more = (170 - 35) = 135

Percentage = 135/35 × 100 = 385.714% ≈ 385.7%

**∴ The required percentage is 385.7%**
